title: Quasi-compact universally subtrusive descent of quasi-compact etale spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], their sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A space is quasi-compact if its point space has a finite subcover for every open cover; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback to every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source. On scheme affine charts the constructible topology is generated by quasi-compact opens and their complements; on an algebraic space $X$ give $|X|$ the final (quotient) topology of the constructible topologies of its representable etale affine scheme charts, as in Rydh Remark (1.8). Call $p:H'\to H$ universally subtrusive if for every affine scheme $T$ and morphism $T\to H$, the point map of $H'\times_HT\to T$ is surjective and a quotient map for the constructible topologies, and every specialization pair $t_0\in\overline{\{t_1\}}$ in $|T|$ lifts to a pair $t'_0\in\overline{\{t'_1\}}$ in $|H'\times_HT|$. Let $p$ be quasi-compact and universally subtrusive, with $H,H'$ quasi-separated. Let $E'\to H'$ be quasi-compact and chartwise etale [def-sfb-space-chartwise-etale-morphism] [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], with $E'$ quasi-separated. Suppose an isomorphism $\theta:p_1^*E'\xrightarrow{\sim}p_2^*E'$ over $H'\times_HH'$ is the identity on the diagonal and satisfies $p_{23}^*\theta\circ p_{12}^*\theta=p_{13}^*\theta$ on the triple fibre product. Then there exist a quasi-separated algebraic space $E$, a quasi-compact chartwise etale map $E\to H$, and an isomorphism $E\times_HH'\simeq E'$ identifying the canonical datum with $\theta$. In particular, the universal-subtrusiveness hypothesis holds whenever $p$ is universally open and surjective on point spaces. No flatness or finite-presentation hypothesis on $p$ is required.

source.place: Rydh, author version 2010-03-03, Theorem (5.17), printed p.22, object-effectivity assertion for E_qc; Definition (2.2) and Remark (2.5)(2c), printed pp.7--8, give the stated hypothesis and universally open sufficient condition. Remark (5.2), printed p.18, extends the base category to quasi-separated algebraic spaces. Read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Use $\mathcal F(B)$ for finitely presented chartwise etale spaces over a quasi-separated base $B$. This is the quasi-compact etale category used here: etaleness gives local finite presentation on charts by [lem-kun-etale-lfp]. Let $X\to B$ be quasi-compact chartwise etale with $X$ quasi-separated, and let $T\to B$ be an affine scheme test, $X_T=X\times_BT$. Then $X_T$ is quasi-compact. By [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] applied to $T\to B$ ($T$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $B$ quasi-separated), $T\to B$ is quasi-separated, hence so is its base change $X_T\to X$; the absolute diagonal of $X_T$ factors as the relative diagonal of $X_T\to X$ followed by the base change of the absolute diagonal of $X$, so $X_T$ is quasi-separated. Now [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] applied to $X_T\to T$ shows that $X_T\to T$ is quasi-separated; as the relative diagonal of $X\to B$ pulls back to that of $X_T\to T$ and quasi-compactness is tested on affine scheme tests, $X\to B$ is quasi-separated. Conversely a finitely presented space over a quasi-separated base has quasi-separated source: factor its absolute diagonal as the relative diagonal followed by the base change of the base's absolute diagonal. Both arrows are quasi-compact, so their composite is quasi-compact (pull back an affine test and use finite subcovers successively). This also explains the source quasi-separatedness assertions below. The meaning of finite presentation is the one spelled out in [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality].

source.place: Notation (5.1), Remark (5.2); expand the identification of E_qc with the finite-presentation etale category

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-subtrusive-topological-descent-calculus], $p$ is universally submersive. Thus [lem-sfb-submersive-etale-space-morphism-descent] supplies full faithfulness, including descent of isomorphisms and detection of equalities, for every base change of $p$. The same applies to any universally subtrusive map considered below. It is the source of uniqueness when assembling local realizations, not a claim that full faithfulness alone constructs an object.

source.place: Proposition (5.3) and Corollary (1.5), as used by (5.6)--(5.8)

proof.text: First establish effective $\mathcal F$-descent for a surjective flat finitely presented map $a:V\to T$ of quasi-separated schemes, after every quasi-separated scheme base change. A datum in $\mathcal F(V)$ is of finite type, so [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-fppf-effectivity] realizes its underlying algebraic space over $T$, with the specified cocycle. Apply [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent] to descend chartwise etaleness, and [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] to descend finite presentation; step 1 gives the required absolute quasi-separatedness. These two descent statements impose no quasi-separatedness assumption on the previously constructed space. Full faithfulness follows by the sheaf realization statement [lem-sfb-fppf-space-datum-sheaf-realization], whose arrows are precisely compatible maps. All these arguments commute with base change, so $a$ is universal effective descent in the sense of [lem-sfb-etale-descent-composition-refinement-calculus].

source.place: Proposition (5.11), realized by the existing Stacks fppf algebraic-space descent and property-locality statements

proof.text: Let $f:V\to T$ be a universally subtrusive finitely presented morphism of affine schemes. By [lem-sfb-subtrusive-fp-flat-proper-refinement], choose $V_1\xrightarrow{a}T_1\xrightarrow{b}T$ and $u:V_1\to V$ with $fu=ba$, where $a$ is faithfully flat of finite presentation and $b$ is proper surjective of finite presentation. Step 3 makes $a$ universal effective $\mathcal F$-descent. For $b$, [lem-sfb-proper-surjection-etale-space-effectivity] gives object effectivity for this same category, and full faithfulness is [lem-sfb-submersive-etale-space-morphism-descent]: a proper surjection is a universal quotient map because it is universally closed and surjective. Properness and finite presentation persist by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], and surjectivity persists by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], so $b$ too is universal effective descent. Apply the composition clause of [lem-sfb-etale-descent-composition-refinement-calculus] to $ba$, and then its right-factor clause to $fu$. This proves that $f$ is universal effective descent; $u$ itself need not be flat, surjective, or effective descent.

source.place: Theorem (5.17), last two sentences: Theorem (3.10), Propositions (5.6),(5.11), Corollary (5.16)

proof.text: Now let $f:V\to T$ be universally subtrusive with $V,T$ affine, without finite presentation. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-fp-limit], write $V=\varprojlim_iV_i$ over $T$, indexed by a small nonempty directed set, with $V_i\to T$ affine finitely presented. These spaces are schemes since affine maps are representable. Each $f_i:V_i\to T$ is universally subtrusive: $f$ factors through $f_i$, so use the right-factor assertion of [lem-sfb-subtrusive-topological-descent-calculus]. In particular no persistence of subtrusiveness under limits is being assumed. Step 4 applies separately to every $f_i$. For a datum $(Z,\theta)$ over $V/T$, $Z\to V$ is finitely presented by step 1.

source.place: Theorem (5.17), reduction by Proposition (5.8); affine finite-presentation approximation is Stacks Tag 0870

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-fp-space-limit-category] to descend $Z$ to a finitely presented $Z_i\to V_i$. Use [lem-sfb-space-etaleness-eventual-stage] to make $Z_i\to V_i$ etale at a later index. Apply the morphism and equality clauses of [lem-sfb-fp-space-limit-category] over the affine systems $V_i\times_TV_i$ and $V_i\times_TV_i\times_TV_i$: descend both $\theta$ and its inverse, then make their two inverse equations, the diagonal identity, and the triple cocycle hold at one common later index. The affine limits exist by [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages]. A map into their pair system is exactly two compatible maps to the $V_i$ with equal images in $T$, hence two maps to $V$ with equal images in $T$; the same argument with three maps handles the triple system. Thus their limits are the corresponding products of $V$. Thus the resulting $(Z_j,\theta_j)$ is an actual descent datum over $V_j/T$ whose pullback is the original specified datum. Every space whose morphisms are descended is finitely presented, all bases are affine qcqs, and only finitely many equations are imposed, so directedness supplies the common index.

source.place: Proposition (5.8), proof: descend object, isomorphism and cocycle; Stacks Tags 07SK and 07SL

proof.text: Step 4 realizes $(Z_j,\theta_j)$ by $E_T\in\mathcal F(T)$ and a specified isomorphism $E_T\times_TV_j\simeq Z_j$. Pull back this isomorphism along $V\to V_j$. It gives $E_T\times_TV\simeq Z$, and its two overlap pullbacks identify the canonical datum with $\theta$ because the datum itself was descended in step 6. This proves the affine-scheme case without any flatness or finite-presentation assumption on $f$.

source.place: Conclusion of Proposition (5.8) in the proof of Theorem (5.17)

proof.text: To pass to algebraic-space sources over an affine scheme $T\to H$ which is an etale chart, put $B'=H'\times_HT$ and $Z'=E'\times_HT$. Base-change stability of quasi-compactness in [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests], and the diagonal factorization in step 1, give $B'$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $Z'\to B'$ quasi-compact etale with quasi-separated source. Choose an affine representable etale surjection $v:V\to B'$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. It is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence]. By [lem-sfb-subtrusive-topological-descent-calculus], $V\to T$ is universally subtrusive (compose $v$ with the base change of $p$). Restrict the datum to $V/T$ and apply steps 5--7. Obtain $E_T\in\mathcal F(T)$ and $E_T\times_TV\simeq Z'\times_{B'}V$. This isomorphism respects the datum on $V\times_{B'}V$, since that datum is the restriction of the one on $V\times_TV$. The full-faithfulness clause of [lem-sfb-etale-space-single-cover-effective-descent] for $v$ therefore descends it to $E_T\times_TB'\simeq Z'$. Its compatibility with $\theta$ is checked after the etale cover $V\times_TV\to B'\times_TB'$ by the same full-faithfulness clause. The quasi-separatedness and base-change assertions used here are the relative-diagonal factorization of step 1 and [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]; finiteness over $T$ makes each source test quasi-compact.

source.place: Theorem (5.17), first reduction replacing the source by an affine etale cover; Remark (5.2)

proof.text: Choose an etale presentation $W\to H$ whose source is a disjoint union of affine schemes, using [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. Step 8 gives realizations $E_a$ over its affine components $W_a$. Form $\coprod_a E_a\to\coprod_aW_a=W$ using [lem-trf-algebraic-space-coproduct] and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The scheme coproducts of their atlases lie in the fixed universe bound [def-weil-size-convention]; all families here are indexed by the set of atlas components. On a disjoint union etaleness and finite presentation hold componentwise: each affine test meets finitely many components, so quasi-compactness and the diagonal condition reduce to a finite union of the corresponding component tests. On their double overlaps, the two realizations have isomorphic pullbacks to $H'$ via their specified identifications with $E'$. By step 2 these comparison isomorphisms descend uniquely; their cocycle and identity follow by faithfulness. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-space-single-cover-effective-descent] (to the disjoint-union presentation, componentwise) to obtain an etale algebraic space $E\to H$. The local identifications with $E'$ glue by its morphism clause and recover precisely $\theta$. To check finite presentation, pull back to any affine scheme $Q\to H$. The scheme etale covering $Q\times_HW\to Q$ pulls the map back to the already finitely presented local maps. The finite-presentation clause of [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], applied over $Q$, proves finite presentation of $E_Q\to Q$. Hence $E\to H$ is quasi-compact and relatively quasi-separated; since $H$ is quasi-separated, step 1 proves that $E$ is absolutely quasi-separated. The empty base gives the empty space and is included.

source.place: Theorem (5.17), affine-base locality and Remark (5.2): gluing along the etale presentation; no use of the downstream Theorem (5.19)

proof.text: Finally, if $p$ is universally open and surjective, [lem-sfb-subtrusive-topological-descent-calculus](2) verifies exactly the affine-test universal-subtrusiveness hypothesis. The proof then applies unchanged. Quasi-compactness of $p$ is used to obtain the affine source refinement in step 8; no flatness or finite-presentation condition on $p$ entered the construction.

lean.statement: theorem quasiCompact_subtrusive_etale_descent {S : Scheme.{u}} (H H' : AlgebraicSpace S) (p : H' ⟶ H) (_hH : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated H) (_hH' : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated H') : (MapIsQuasiCompact p.hom.hom → MapIsUniversallySubtrusive p.hom.hom → ∀ (E' : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : E' ⟶ H'), MapIsQuasiCompact f.hom.hom → IsChartwiseEtale f → IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated E' → ∀ D : Over.DescentDatum p (Over.mk f), ∃ (E : AlgebraicSpace S) (g : E ⟶ H) (q : E' ⟶ E), IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated E ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact g.hom.hom ∧ IsChartwiseEtale g ∧ IsPullback q f g p ∧ ∀ (T : AlgebraicSpace S) (a b : T ⟶ H') (h : a ≫ p = b ≫ p) (x : Over.mk a ⟶ Over.mk f), (D.transport a b h x).left ≫ q = x.left ≫ q) ∧ (MapIsUniversallyOpen p → Function.Surjective (mapPoint p.hom.hom) → MapIsUniversallySubtrusive p.hom.hom)
